title: Validation, Release Gates, and Rollback
summary: Evidence already collected and what still gates release.

content.text: Plain summary

The software side is well tested for a candidate, but the physical printer gates still matter most. The next approval step is not trust, it is proof: boot recovery, image eMMC, verify restore path, then commission with you present.
Evidence already collected
Current repository test suite: 324 unit tests passed, including exact Orca 2.4.2 calibration-contract tests.
Publishable-tree and secret scans passed with no private GerGo package, credentials, backups, generated G-code, or printer images in the public candidate.
Diff hygiene: git diff --check passed after the rebase.
Candidate v13 evidence records 29 exact pinned Klipper v0.13 production cases and 11 vendor Klipper 0.12 compatibility cases.
The validation report records the private GerGo package absent from the public stage.
Refinement validation evidence

The fresh v13 commissioning stage manifest has SHA-256 fcbe23e6031a9066935f8d2c7a4d923962f69ab4f63225fc8b90f58fce504756. The final validation report has SHA-256 d636597368a563f1ed45a0dbb1deb752857e65b4d8f542973c9a2242fd5cf950 and passes all eleven repository, policy, large-print admission, exact Klipper v0.13, vendor Klipper v0.12, UI, lifecycle, host-network, systemd, secret, and staging checks.

The large-format gate admitted a deterministic 900-layer, 250 x 234 x 270 mm digital job representing about 1.5 kg of PLA and 36,000 retract, wipe, and recovery cycles through the exact v13 staged scanner, protected snapshot, and approval-record path. It also rejected repeated stationary-extrusion and microscopic-move allowance-farming attacks. This proves scale-safe policy behavior; it does not simulate real heater, probe, motion, material, or frame physics.

Exact Orca 2.4.2 normal slices were generated for the camera bracket and both Frieren process candidates. All three completed and were accepted by the scanner. Their evidence hashes are 2a313d... for the bracket, 59c9bf... for Frieren quality, and 1bf620... for Frieren easier release. Generated G-code was deliberately excluded from the delivery.

Orca 2.4.2 calibration compatibility is pinned to source commit 8500fcdccaa10b5099ac20d252af3a7c560046f1. Tests admit the expected temperature, maximum-volumetric-speed, pressure-advance, flow-ratio, and retraction forms, while proving unsafe temperature, position, pressure-advance, flow-override, tuning-tower, and unmatched stationary-extrusion variants fail.

Software evidence is not physical acceptance. No heater, motor, probe, camera, network soak, calibration, or print result has been claimed by these local tests. Those remain attended owner gates after recovery and installation.
Release gates still open
Boot recovery USB three times and prove the eMMC is not mounted as root.
Capture, hash, validate, and read-only inspect the entire stock eMMC image.
Download/checksum complete Comgrow 1.5.2 recovery material.
Test guarded image inspect, capture, verify, and write commands without touching the real target until approved.
Boot the candidate from USB with printer control disabled and prove screen, touch, fan, Ethernet, Wi-Fi, USB, camera, storage, and service permissions.
Only after recovery proof, write candidate image to eMMC.
Establish MCU communication without movement or heat.
Flash MCUs only after exact original recovery firmware and bootloader settings are proven.
Commission with attended sensor, fan, endstop, probe, axis, heater, communication-loss, and emergency-stop checks.
Recalibrate PID, rotation distance, GerGo alignment, probe repeatability, Z offset, mesh, input shaping, temperature, flow, pressure advance, retraction, and volumetric flow.
Print a standard first-layer test and a small dimensional print before camera bracket or Frieren approval.

attrs.title: usb vs alternatives
attrs.instruction: explain if it would be possible to run these tests and apply the new firmware over natwork from this device rather than from the usb so you always can run diagnostics immediately?  Or will that be impossible due to network capabilities even when the printer is on ethernet getting disabled when we mess with firmware?
attrs.resolution: Answered in USB versus network during migration: the design uses USB for an independent boot/root safety base and Ethernet for diagnostics, capture, restore, and bounded transfers. Rewriting the live eMMC OS over its own network stack is the unsafe case.

content.text: USB versus network during migration
Short answer: the safe migration uses both. USB is the independent boot root; direct Ethernet is the diagnostics and data-transfer path while that known recovery system is running.

Network is useful and expected for diagnostics. Once the printer is booted into the marked recovery USB, the laptop can inspect the board, stream the eMMC image, verify hashes, and restore a matching image over direct Ethernet.

USB is still needed because the eMMC is the disk we are trying to back up or replace. If the printer is booted from eMMC and we rewrite that same eMMC, the operating system, network config, SSH service, and files being used to do the write can disappear or corrupt mid-operation.
The recovery USB keeps the printer running from a disk that is not being written. If an Ethernet transfer fails, the recovery system is still alive and the operation can be restarted safely.

The candidate also has a restricted key-only transport for reviewed configuration bundles after the system is installed and idle. That is for bounded updates, not for blindly replacing the root operating system while it is running.
Maintenance mode intentionally has no network. That is a safety choice: bypass tools live in a local-only configuration, not behind a web UI or LAN endpoint.

Practical meaning for you: you should still have immediate diagnostics from this laptop during recovery because the laptop talks to the USB-booted printer over direct Ethernet. The unsafe path is depending on the old or half-replaced eMMC network stack as the only control plane.
Rollback

Rollback means booting recovery USB, restoring the verified stock eMMC image over Ethernet, restoring original MCU firmware if it was changed, and verifying stock Comgrow 1.5.2 before any movement. A rollback drill is part of release, not an optional comfort step.
